literal: When Jun learned of it afterward, he said: "To gain wealth and lose conduct—what I will not take."
idiomatic: When Jun learned of it later he said, "Wealth gained, conduct lost—that I will not take."

literal: He sought out the buyer and returned it.
idiomatic: He found the buyer and returned the silk.

literal: By selection he became a mourning attendant for Emperor Xiaowen and was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.
idiomatic: Selected as a mourning attendant for Xiaowen, he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance.

literal: When the Dacheng bandits rose and Yan and Zhao were thrown into disorder, Jun joined the staff on the eastern campaign; for merit he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: When Dacheng rebels threw Yan and Zhao into turmoil, Jun served on the eastern staff and was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant for merit.

literal: He was promoted in succession to Chief Clerk in the Minister of Works office.
idiomatic: He rose in turn to Chief Clerk in the Minister of Works office.

literal: At the time Empress Ling held court, cut salaries of officeholders by a tenth, and built Yongning Buddhist Temple, putting Jun in charge of it.
idiomatic: While Empress Ling held court she cut official salaries by a tenth and built Yongning Temple, putting Jun in charge.

literal: Costs ran to tens of millions, yet the chief clerks could not conceal anything from him.
idiomatic: Costs ran to tens of millions; chief clerks could not hide a thing from him.

literal: When the temple was finished, it was also magnificently grand.
idiomatic: When the temple stood complete, it was magnificently grand.

literal: Empress Ling praised him and appointed him General of the Left Army.
idiomatic: Empress Ling praised him and made him General of the Left Army.

literal: In the Xiaochang era the court debated that state revenue was insufficient and therefore established a Salt-Pool Commandant, rank equal to a superior commandery.
idiomatic: In Xiaochang the court, finding revenue short, established a Salt-Pool Commandant equal in rank to a superior commandery.

literal: Those who held the post before and after often embezzled; Jun was therefore put in it while still chief clerk.
idiomatic: Earlier holders had often embezzled; Jun was appointed while still chief clerk.

literal: At the beginning of Yongan, a man of Huazhou named Shi Di sued Minister of Works Yang Chun over fields.
idiomatic: At the start of Yongan, Shi Di of Huazhou sued Minister of Works Yang Chun over land.

literal: The chief administrator, because Chun was powerful and noble, all said Chun was in the right and wished to give the fields to Chun.
idiomatic: The chief administrator, seeing Chun's power, all sided with him and meant to award the land to Chun.

literal: Jun said: "Shi Di is a poor man; Lord Yang seized his land by force. If you would harm the insufficient to enrich the ample, and make me echo the crowd, I dare not obey."
idiomatic: Jun said, "Shi Di is a poor man whom Lord Yang robbed. To strip the wanting to feed the full, and make me echo the crowd—I dare not obey."

literal: He therefore returned the land to Shi Di.
idiomatic: The land was returned to Shi Di.

literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang learned of it afterward and praised Jun for holding firm without bending; he was made Marshal.
idiomatic: Xiaozhuang learned of it and praised Jun's upright refusal; he was made Marshal.

literal: Those who had sided with Chun all blamed him.
idiomatic: Those who had sided with Chun blamed Jun.

literal: In the second year he went out as Inspector of Liang Province.
idiomatic: In year two he went out as Inspector of Liang.

literal: The people were wild and rough; many became bandits.
idiomatic: Custom was wild; banditry was common.

literal: Jun then ordered the commanderies and counties to establish schools, urged them to plow and raise silkworms, and taught them through ritual and yielding.
idiomatic: He ordered schools built, urged farming and sericulture, and taught courtesy and yielding.

literal: Within several years custom was suddenly transformed.
idiomatic: Within years custom was transformed.

literal: Liang sent its general Cao Yanzhi to hold Weixing, piling ramparts day after day.
idiomatic: Liang sent Cao Yanzhi to hold Weixing, raising ramparts daily.

literal: Yanzhi repeatedly harassed the border; frontier people were troubled.
idiomatic: Yanzhi harried the frontier; border folk suffered.

literal: Jun sent Chief Administrator Du Lindao to storm the city and capture Yanzhi as well.
idiomatic: Jun sent Chief Administrator Du Lindao to take the city and capture Yanzhi.

literal: Yanzhi was the youngest brother of Liang's great general Xiao Jingzong.
idiomatic: Yanzhi was youngest brother to Liang's great general Xiao Jingzong.

literal: Thereupon the men of Liang were afraid.
idiomatic: The Liang were afraid.

literal: As Wei affairs were many and the province remote, the Liang knew there was no outside aid and massed troops at Weixing, intent on taking it.
idiomatic: With Wei in turmoil and the province remote, Liang knew no aid would come and massed at Weixing to take it.

literal: Jun comforted and roused his officers and men; all thought to give their lives.
idiomatic: Jun comforted his troops; all wished to die for him.

literal: The Liang, knowing he had won the hearts of the masses, did not dare press him.
idiomatic: Knowing he held the army's hearts, Liang did not dare press him.

literal: Jun in the province lived plainly and did not pursue estates; his sons and the rest all walked home on foot.
idiomatic: Jun lived plainly in the province, built no estates; his sons walked home on foot.

literal: Officials and people escorted Jun and lingered on the road; only after long time did he cross the border.
idiomatic: Officials and people escorted him, lingering on the road long before he left the border.

literal: In the third year of Datong, Eastern Wei appointed Jun Inspector of Luozhou; Jun therefore plotted to return to court.
idiomatic: In Datong year three Eastern Wei made him Inspector of Luoyang; he plotted to return to court.

literal: In the fifth year he brought his household and four hundred kin into the Pass and was made Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: In year five he brought family and four hundred kin through the Pass and was made Director of the Secretariat.

literal: At the time the army and state were newly founded and classics scattered; Jun first selected clerks to copy and gather the canon—gradually the four divisions of books became fairly complete.
idiomatic: With the state newly founded and classics scattered, Jun chose clerks to copy books; the four divisions grew fairly complete.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed Baron of Anxi County.
idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and Baron of Anxi.

literal: In the seventeenth year he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then claimed grave illness and no longer attended court.
idiomatic: In year seventeen he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then pleaded grave illness and stopped attending court.

literal: In the third year of Gongdi he was granted the surname Ruokouyin.
idiomatic: In Gongdi year three he was granted the surname Ruokouyin.

literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, his rank was advanced to viscount.
idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne his rank rose to viscount.

literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the privilege of the same rites as the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: In Wucheng year one he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Three-Duke rites.

literal: Though Jun's years were high, his will and understanding had not declined.
idiomatic: Though old, his mind had not declined.

literal: In teaching his sons and grandsons he always began with ritual and propriety.
idiomatic: Teaching sons and grandsons, he always began with ritual.

literal: Emperor Ming honored Confucian learning and prized virtue and especially admired him, repeatedly bestowing favors and wishing to see him.
idiomatic: Ming honored learning and virtue, admired him, sent gifts, and wished to see him.

literal: Jun could not refuse and entered court; the emperor sat with him on the same mat and asked about old stories of Luoyang.
idiomatic: Jun entered court; the emperor shared his mat and asked about Luoyang of old.

literal: Jun was eight feet tall, beard and whiskers snow-white, bearing dignified and composed, voice clear and bright.
idiomatic: Eight feet tall, beard snow-white, bearing composed, voice clear.

literal: In discussion with him the emperor unconsciously shifted forward on his knees again and again.
idiomatic: In talk with him the emperor, without noticing, drew his knees forward again and again.

literal: When Jun took leave to return, the emperor personally held his hand and said: "Sir, your years and virtue are both honored—what I admire in you.
idiomatic: When Jun left, the emperor held his hand and said, "Your years and virtue are both honored—that is what I admire.

literal: Matters of begging your counsel are what I hope from you.
idiomatic: I look to you for counsel.

literal: You should often come to see me, to ease my empty longing."
idiomatic: Come often, to ease my longing."

literal: He had the imperial carriage wait for Jun to ride out before the emperor.
idiomatic: He had the imperial carriage brought for Jun to ride out before him.

literal: Turning to those at his side he said: "Such things only one who has long accumulated goodness can attain.
idiomatic: He told his attendants, "Only long-accumulated goodness wins such things.

literal: How much more than being honored today—it will be handed down ten thousand ages."
idiomatic: More than honor today—it will live ten thousand ages."

literal: Men of the time all considered it glory.
idiomatic: All the age called it glory.

literal: He died at eighty-two.
idiomatic: He died at eighty-two.

literal: Emperor Wu sighed in regret and posthumously granted his former offices, adding Overseer of Military Affairs for Ji, Ding, and Ying Provinces and Inspector of Ji, posthumous name Yuan.
idiomatic: Wu sighed, granted his former offices, added Overseer of Ji, Ding, and Ying and Inspector of Ji, posthumous name Yuan.

literal: Jun was devoted to humaneness and righteousness; among those within mourning obligation who were orphaned and young, in food and clothing plenty or want he shared alike with them.
idiomatic: Devoted to humaneness, he shared food and clothing with orphaned kin within mourning obligation.

literal: In youth he was known to Minister of Works Cui Guang; Guang ordered his son Li to befriend Jun.
idiomatic: In youth Cui Guang knew him and ordered his son Li to befriend Jun.

literal: Whenever Jun visited Guang they would talk in pure conversation until the day moved on.
idiomatic: Whenever Jun visited Guang they talked until the day was gone.

literal: Junior Preceptor of the Clan Lu Bian, because Jun's achievement and conduct were both lofty, treated him with the rites due teacher and friend.
idiomatic: Lu Bian, seeing Jun's conduct lofty, treated him as teacher and friend.

literal: Whenever he had leisure he would go to Jun and feast in talk a whole day.
idiomatic: In leisure he feasted and talked with Jun whole days.

literal: He would always tell people: "If I do not see Lord Anxi, vexation will not leave me."
idiomatic: He said, "Without Lord Anxi, vexation never leaves."

literal: Such was the esteem in which the learned world held him.
idiomatic: So the learned world esteemed him.

literal: His son Feng reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with army credentials, Administrator of Shunyang, Inspector of Xun, and Duke of Changguo.
idiomatic: Son Feng reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with army credentials, Shunyang Administrator, Xun Inspector, Duke of Changguo.

literal: Feng's younger brother Yong was fond of learning and most famed.
idiomatic: Younger brother Yong loved learning and was most famed.

literal: In mourning he was destroyed by grief.
idiomatic: In mourning grief destroyed him.

literal: He held Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with army credentials, Lower Grand Masters for Court, Proclamation of Laws, and Sacrificial Rites, Junior Remonstrator, and Duke of Huoze.
idiomatic: He held army credentials as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, lower grand masters for court, law, and sacrifice, Junior Remonstrator, Duke of Huoze.

literal: Li Fan, styled Shize, was a man of Zhuolu in Fanyang.
idiomatic: Li Fan, styled Shize, came from Zhuolu in Fanyang.

literal: His grandfather Shao was Administrator of Puyang under Murong Bao; he welcomed the surrender of the commandery and Daowu made him Overseer of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Grandfather Shao was Puyang Administrator under Murong Bao; he welcomed surrender and Daowu made him Overseer of Yan.

literal: His father Song was Administrator of Tianshui.
idiomatic: Father Song was Tianshui Administrator.

literal: Fan, in Emperor Taiwu's time, was attendant in the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: In Taiwu's time Fan served the Eastern Palace.

literal: When Taiwu took the throne he recorded old merit of the former court and granted the rank Baron of Yongning.
idiomatic: When Taiwu took the throne he recorded prior merit and made Fan Baron of Yongning.

literal: As Director of Ceremonial Offerings he escorted the spirit tablets of Taiwu and Jingmu to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to viscount.
idiomatic: As Director of Ceremonial Offerings he escorted Taiwu and Jingmu to the temple and was advanced to viscount.

literal: He was Chief Clerk to Grand General of the South Murong Baiyao.
idiomatic: He was Chief Clerk to Grand General of the South Murong Baiyao.

literal: When the Three Qi were pacified Fan offered many plans; Baiyao used all his stratagems and therefore memorialized him as Inspector of Qing.
idiomatic: When the Three Qi fell Fan offered many plans; Baiyao used them all and memorialized him Inspector of Qing.

literal: He was advanced to marquis, made Champion General, and returned as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Advanced to marquis and Champion General, he returned Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing, with acting title Duke of Fanyang.
idiomatic: Later he was General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qing, acting Duke of Fanyang.

literal: When Fan earlier left his province and returned to the capital, at night he dreamed of dark hair brushing his ankle.
idiomatic: When Fan earlier left the province for the capital he dreamed dark hair brushed his ankle.

literal: Another day he spoke of it.
idiomatic: Another day he told the dream.

literal: At the time a man of Qi skilled in dream-reading, Shi Wujin, said: "My lord, your splendor already lies below Qi."
idiomatic: A Qi dream-reader, Shi Wujin, said, "My lord, your splendor already lies below Qi."

literal: "When my lord oversees and comforts Eastern Qin, your light covers the sea and Mount Tai—you will surely again shepherd all Qi and receive a second fief at Yingqiu."
idiomatic: "When you oversee Eastern Qin and your light covers sea and Mount Tai, you will again shepherd all Qi and receive Yingqiu a second time."

literal: Fan laughed and replied: "I will make this dream come true for you."
idiomatic: Fan laughed, "I will make this dream true for you."

literal: It turned out as he said.
idiomatic: It came to pass as he said.

literal: At the time the garrison commander Yuan Yili memorialized that Fan trafficked with outside bandits.
idiomatic: Garrison commander Yuan Yili reported Fan trafficked with outside bandits.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen edicted Fan: "Garrison commander Yili reports that you built ships and bought jade, trafficked with outside bandits, plotted to frame you, and eyed your provincial post.
idiomatic: Xiaowen edicted, "Yili says you built ships and bought jade, trafficked with bandits, framed you, and coveted your province.

literal: The offices investigated; truth and falsehood will show themselves—the guilty have now paid their crime.
idiomatic: Investigation will show truth; the guilty have paid.

literal: You should plan clearly and not doubt again."
idiomatic: Plan clearly and doubt no more."

literal: He returned to court and died in the capital.
idiomatic: He returned to court and died in the capital.

literal: Posthumous name Mu.
idiomatic: Posthumous name Mu.

literal: His son Daoyuan.
idiomatic: Son Daoyuan.

literal: Daoyuan, styled Shanchang.
idiomatic: Daoyuan, styled Shanchang.

literal: At first he inherited the rank Marquis of Yongning; by rule it was reduced to baron.
idiomatic: He first inherited Marquis of Yongning; by rule it fell to baron.

literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, because Daoyuan in enforcing law was pure and severe, drew him from the Grand Tutor's staff as Secretary Attendant Censor.
idiomatic: Censor Li Biao, finding Daoyuan pure and severe in law, drew him from the Grand Tutor's staff as Secretary Attendant Censor.

literal: When Biao was impeached by Vice Director Li Chong, Daoyuan as subordinate official was dismissed by association.
idiomatic: When Biao was impeached by Vice Director Li Chong, Daoyuan as subordinate was dismissed with him.

literal: In the Jingming era he was Chief Administrator of the Pacify-the-East office in Ji Province.
idiomatic: In Jingming he was Chief Administrator of the Pacify-the-East office in Ji.

literal: Inspector Yu Jin was father of the Shun empress; he campaigned west into Guanzhong and also did not reach the province—Daoyuan conducted affairs three years.
idiomatic: Inspector Yu Jin was the Shun empress's father; campaigning west he never reached the province—Daoyuan ran affairs three years.

literal: His government was harsh and cruel; officials and people feared him; thieves fled to other regions.
idiomatic: Government was harsh; officials and people feared him; thieves fled elsewhere.

literal: Later on probation he held Luoyang Commandery; Daoyuan memorialized to establish schools and honor and urge learning and teaching.
idiomatic: Later acting Administrator of Luoyang, he memorialized for schools and honored learning.

literal: The edict said: "Luoyang was originally because of barbarians that no great academy was established.
idiomatic: The edict said, "Luoyang, being barbarian country, had no great academy.

literal: Now permission is granted, to complete the good administrator Wen Weng's transformation."
idiomatic: Now it is permitted, to finish Wen Weng's transformation."

literal: In the commandery Daoyuan, the mountain barbarians submitted to his fierce name and did not dare raid.
idiomatic: In the commandery mountain tribes submitted to his name and did not raid.

literal: In the Yanchang era he was Inspector of Eastern Jing; his fierce government was as in Ji Province.
idiomatic: In Yanchang he was Eastern Jing Inspector; government was fierce as in Ji.
